title: 航空構造設計Ⅰ
subtitle: Aircraft Structure Design I
keywords: Stress and strain 2.Plane stress and plane strain 3.Torsion, bending, and tension 4.Short column 5.Long column
educationalGoal: Students will learn (1) relationship between stress and strain of 3D elastic body (2) plane stress and plane strain (2D theory of elasticity) (3) slender bar under torsional, bending, and tensile load (4) short column under eccentric compression load (5) buckling of long column under compression load
advice: On the basis of knowledge learned in subjects such as ‘Mechanics of Materials’ and ‘Mechanics of Aircraft Structure’, student will learn the advanced mechanics for aircraft structural design. We will cover the following materials: (1) relationship between stress and strain of 3D elastic body (2) plane stress and plane strain (constitutive equation in 2D theory of elasticity) (3) stress of bar under combination of torsional, bending, and tensile load (4) stress of short column under eccentric compression load (5) buckling of long column under compression load Students should thoroughly review what they have learned in ‘Mechanics of Materials’ and ‘Mechanics of Aircraft Structure’ before taking this course.
books: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials -Second Edition, Kyoritsu Syuppan, 2013
requiredKnowledge: Basic knowledge of Mechanics of Materials and Mechanics of Aircraft Structure.

activityGoals.body: Be able to express the relationship between stresses and strains of 3D elastic body
Be able to explain the difference between plane stress and plane strain
Be able to calculate the maximum principal stress of the bar under both torsional and tensile loads
Be able to calculate the core of section of a short column under eccentric compression load
Be able to calculate the buckling load of long columns with various ends’ conditions

achievementLevels.ideal: 1) Accurately express the relationship between stresses and strains of 3D elastic body using only Young’s modulus and Poisson’s ratio 2) Fully understand the difference between plane stress and plane strain 3) Calculate the maximum principal stress and the maximum shear stress of the bar under both torsional and tensile loads 4) Calculate the core of section of a short column under eccentric compression load 5) Calculate the buckling load of long columns with various ends’ conditions
achievementLevels.standard: 1) Express the relationship between stresses and strains of 3D elastic body 2) Understand the difference between plane stress and plane strain 3) Calculate the maximum principal stress of the bar under both torsional and tensile loads 4) Calculate the normal stress of a short column under eccentric compression load 5) Calculate the buckling load of a long column pin-support at both ends.
